Points C and D are on the major arc $\overset{\frown}{BCA}$ (points B, C, D are arranged clockwise), $\overset{\frown}{CD} = \overset{\frown}{AB}$. Point F is a moving point on $\overset{\frown}{CD}$. Connect CF and extend it to intersect the extension line of chord AD at point E. $BC \parallel AD$. As shown in Figure 3, when $\angle B = 90^\circ$ and $CE = 5\sqrt{5}$, connect AC, OE, and let OE intersect $\odot O$ at point K. Calculate the ratio of the area of $\triangle KDE$ to the area of $\triangle EOC$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} In Figure 3, connect $CD$,\\
$\because$ $\angle B=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $AC$ is the diameter of $\odot O$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle ADC=90^\circ$, $AC=2AO=10$,\\
In $Rt\triangle CDE$, $CE=5\sqrt{5}$, $CD=AB=4\sqrt{5}$,\\
$\therefore$ $DE=\sqrt{CE^{2}-CD^{2}}=3\sqrt{5}$,\\
In $Rt\triangle ADC$, $AD=\sqrt{AC^{2}-CD^{2}}=2\sqrt{5}$,\\
$\therefore$ $AE=AD+DE=5\sqrt{5}$,\\
$\therefore$ $AE=CE$, thus $\triangle AEC$ is an isosceles triangle,\\
$\because$ $AO=OC$,\\
$\therefore$ $OE\perp AC$,\\
In $Rt\triangle AOE$, $OE=\sqrt{AE^{2}-OA^{2}}=\sqrt{(5\sqrt{5})^{2}-5^{2}}=10$,\\
$\therefore$ $KE=OE-OK=5$,\\
Draw $KM\perp DE$ at M through point K, then $\angle KME=\angle AOE=90^\circ$, and also $\angle KEM=\angle AEO$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle KME\sim \triangle AOE$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{KM}{AO}=\frac{KE}{AE}$, that is $\frac{KM}{5}=\frac{5}{5\sqrt{5}}$,\\
Solving for $KM$, we get: $KM=\sqrt{5}$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{S_{\triangle KDE}}{S_{\triangle EOC}}=\frac{\frac{1}{2}DE\cdot KM}{\frac{1}{2}OC\cdot OE}=\frac{3\sqrt{5}\times \sqrt{5}}{5\times 10}=\boxed{\frac{3}{10}}$.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in Figure 1, it is known that the radius of $\odot O$ is 5, and the chord $AB = 4\sqrt{5}$. Points C and D are on the major arc $\overset{\frown}{BCA}$ (points B, C, D are arranged clockwise), $\overset{\frown}{CD} = \overset{\frown}{AB}$. Point F is a moving point on $\overset{\frown}{CD}$. Connect CF and extend it to intersect the extension line of chord AD at point E. $BC \parallel AD$. As shown in Figure 3, when $\angle B = 90^\circ$ and $CE = 5\sqrt{5}$, connect AC, OE, and let OE intersect $\odot O$ at point K. Calculate the ratio of the area of $\triangle KDE$ to the area of $\triangle EOC$.
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} In Figure 3, connect $CD$,\\
$\because$ $\angle B=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $AC$ is the diameter of $\odot O$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle ADC=90^\circ$, $AC=2AO=10$,\\
In $Rt\triangle CDE$, $CE=5\sqrt{5}$, $CD=AB=4\sqrt{5}$,\\
$\therefore$ $DE=\sqrt{CE^{2}-CD^{2}}=3\sqrt{5}$,\\
In $Rt\triangle ADC$, $AD=\sqrt{AC^{2}-CD^{2}}=2\sqrt{5}$,\\
$\therefore$ $AE=AD+DE=5\sqrt{5}$,\\
$\therefore$ $AE=CE$, thus $\triangle AEC$ is an isosceles triangle,\\
$\because$ $AO=OC$,\\
$\therefore$ $OE\perp AC$,\\
In $Rt\triangle AOE$, $OE=\sqrt{AE^{2}-OA^{2}}=\sqrt{(5\sqrt{5})^{2}-5^{2}}=10$,\\
$\therefore$ $KE=OE-OK=5$,\\
Draw $KM\perp DE$ at M through point K, then $\angle KME=\angle AOE=90^\circ$, and also $\angle KEM=\angle AEO$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle KME\sim \triangle AOE$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{KM}{AO}=\frac{KE}{AE}$, that is $\frac{KM}{5}=\frac{5}{5\sqrt{5}}$,\\
Solving for $KM$, we get: $KM=\sqrt{5}$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{S_{\triangle KDE}}{S_{\triangle EOC}}=\frac{\frac{1}{2}DE\cdot KM}{\frac{1}{2}OC\cdot OE}=\frac{3\sqrt{5}\times \sqrt{5}}{5\times 10}=\boxed{\frac{3}{10}}$

$\therefore$ $AE=AD+DE=5\sqrt{5}$,\\

$\because$ $AO=OC$,\\
$\therefore$ $OE\perp AC$,\\
In $Rt\triangle AOE$, $OE=\sqrt{AE^{2}-OA^{2}}=\sqrt{(5\sqrt{5})^{2}-5^{2}}=10$,\\
$\therefore$ $KE=OE-OK=5$,\\
Draw $KM\perp DE$ at M through point K, then $\angle KME=\angle AOE=90^\circ$, and also $\angle KEM=\angle AEO$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle KME\sim \triangle AOE$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{KM}{AO}=\frac{KE}{AE}$, that is $\frac{KM}{5}=\frac{5}{5\sqrt{5}}$,\\
Solving for $KM$, we get: $KM=\sqrt{5}$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{S_{\triangle KDE}}{S_{\triangle EOC}}=\frac{\frac{1}{2}DE\cdot KM}{\frac{1}{2}OC\cdot OE}=\frac{3\sqrt{5}\times \sqrt{5}}{5\times 10}=\boxed{\frac{3}{10}}$
